later_events.mechanism: amendment (strike and insert): section 31 of Executive Order 13286 strikes the words the Secretary of Transportation in section 1 and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92
amendment (restatement): section 1(a) of Executive Order 14131 amends section 1 to read as a new text; the order has no separate effective-date section, so the signing date is used

clauses.reason: Section 1 continues the Presidential Service Certificate, makes its design part of the order, and provides who awards it and to whom, the bar on issuing it to a holder of a Vice Presidential or similar EOP certificate for the same period, and the one-year assignment requirement after January 21, 1989. Two later orders changed its words. Section 31 of Executive Order 13286, effective March 1, 2003, struck the Secretary of Transportation and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security. Section 1(a) of Executive Order 14131, signed December 20, 2024, then amended section 1 to read as a new text: the original text said the Certificate is awarded by the Secretary of the Army, Navy or Air Force or, when the Coast Guard is not operating as a service in the Navy, by the Secretary of Homeland Security (after the 2003 change), to members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force and Coast Guard; the new text says it is awarded to members of the United States Uniformed Services by the Secretary of the military department concerned, by the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when not in the Navy, and by the Secretary of Commerce or of Health and Human Services for members of the commissioned corps of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration or the Public Health Service. The restatement changes the substance of who may receive and award the Certificate, which a human reviewer should note. The clause continues as amended. The held Code note prints the provision as part of the order as amended and no held later order ends it, so it is treated as continuing on 2026-10-14.

clauses.reason: Section 2 continues the Presidential Service Badge, makes its design part of the order, provides that it is awarded to those who have been granted the Certificate in the same manner, and that it is worn as part of the uniform under regulations of the respective Secretaries. Section 1(b) of Executive Order 14131, signed December 20, 2024, amended section 2 to read as a new text; the changes replace the original description of recipients as members of the Armed Forces with members of the United States Uniformed Services and drop the quotation marks around the short name Badge. The restatement changes the class of recipients, which a human reviewer should note. The clause continues as amended. The held Code note prints the provision as part of the order as amended and no held later order ends it, so it is treated as continuing on 2026-10-14.

clauses.mechanism: performance_on_effective_date: self-executing supersession of Executive Order 10879 took effect when the order was issued
clauses.reason: Section 5 provides that the order supersedes Executive Order No. 10879 of June 1, 1960, as amended. The order has no effective-date provision, so the supersession took effect when the order was signed on March 20, 1992 (the Federal Register published it on March 25, 1992 at 57 FR 10281); the alternative reading that it took effect on publication is disclosed. The command was performed on that date and Executive Order 10879 remains superseded; the Code note still prints the sentence, which records the performed supersession and does not show a continuing command. No held source shows an earlier effect or a later revival.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12793 of March 20, 1992 (57 FR 10281, Federal Register Vol. 57 No. 58, Wednesday March 25, 1992) continues the Presidential Service Certificate and the Presidential Service Badge. The held original is the machine-extracted text of the govinfo Federal Register PDF (PDF pages 11-16, which include neighbouring documents) in which the order appears from the title on page 10281 through section 5, the document marker and the White House dateline, so identity and completeness were confirmed against the text. The held U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (CURRENT:EO:12793#0) as amended by section 31 of Executive Order 13286 and section 1 of Executive Order 14131; that is the current predicate for the continuing clauses. Later events were read from the held official Federal Register texts of both orders. Executive Order 13286 section 31 (effective March 1, 2003 by its section 92) replaced Transportation with Homeland Security in section 1. Executive Order 14131 section 1 (signed December 20, 2024) restated sections 1 and 2. Executive Order 13373 of 2005 amends Executive Order 11926 and only refers to section 1 of this order, so it is not a later event for this order. The order has no expiry or contingent end of its own. Sections 1 to 4 continue; section 5 (supersession of Executive Order 10879) was performed on signing.
